Reviewed as Taha (with Claude Code assisting). I merged this branch into current `dev`: no conflicts, `ruff`, `mypy` clean, **294 passed / 1 skipped against a real PostgreSQL 16.10**, so `test_seed_twice_inserts_only_thirty_rows` (the one you could not run) passes: first run 30, second run 0, total 30.

- 30 distinct texts, all six categories and three priorities, fixed `uuid5` ids, `reporter_contact` null, `python -m app.seed` refuses to run without `DATABASE_URL` and disposes the engine. Good use of the repository's `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` insert, so no new SQL.

Two small things, not blockers:
1. `docs/AI-USAGE.md`: my #47 row had landed in the Contributor B table (my append went to the end of the file). Your diff moves it to the right table, which is correct; I am fixing my other two rows the same way, so expect a trivial conflict there and keep both.
2. I will wire `python -m app.seed` into `compose.yaml` (the `migrate` step) myself, since that file is mine until #48 rebases.

Approving.

Reviewed as Taha (with Claude Code assisting). All ten required checks are green on this head. I also merged it into current `dev` locally: `npm ci`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `build` pass and **11 Vitest tests pass** (on my Windows path with a space the default fork pool times out, so I ran `vitest run --pool=threads`; CI on Linux runs the normal command and is green).

- Both findings from my #80 review are fixed and tested: the Dashboard aborts the previous request and ignores stale responses (version counter plus `AbortController`, with a test that a slow older response cannot overwrite a newer filter), and Submit shows `Retry after N seconds` from the `Retry-After` header on a 429 (digits only, so a hostile header cannot inject text).
- `Stats` shows every enum value and `X-Cache` HIT/MISS/Unknown from the response header; the error boundary logs only the error name and component stack, never complaint text; `test` script exists, so the `test-frontend` job now really runs.
- The evidence PNG is described honestly as a mocked `X-Cache: HIT` response, not a live Redis measurement.

Nothing blocking. Approving.

Reviewed as Taha (with Claude Code assisting). All ten required checks are green on this head, including `integration` with your new negative ping step and the frontend size measurements, so I did not re-run locally; I read every file.

What I checked:
- **frontend/Dockerfile:** two stages, pinned `node:22.23.3-alpine3.24` and `nginx:1.27.5-alpine3.21`, only `dist/` reaches runtime, `USER nginx`, port 8080, healthcheck, nginx as PID 1. The CI step asserts no `node`, no `node_modules`, no `src` in the final image.
- **nginx.conf:** non-root safe (pid and temp paths in /tmp), `/api/` proxied to `backend:8000` with `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr` (overwrites the client's value, exactly what the rate limiter needs), SPA fallback.
- **compose.yaml:** frontend on `edge` only; backend still the only bridge; Ollama serving container on `internal` only with the model fetched by a one-shot `ollama-pull` on `edge` (good answer to the `internal: true` question); backend published on loopback only; seed runs after migration.
- **compose.prod.yaml:** no `build:`, no bind mount, no port on the database or cache, `IMAGE_TAG` required (`:?`).

One real defect to fix before #52 (fine as part of that PR): in `compose.prod.yaml` the images are `civicpulse-backend:${IMAGE_TAG}` and `civicpulse-frontend:${IMAGE_TAG}`, but `cd.yml` will publish `ghcr.io/tahasohail-goat/civicpulse-backend:<sha>` (the prod Kustomize overlay already uses those names). As written, `docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up` cannot pull what CD publishes. Use the full GHCR names in both places.

Small notes: the production `migrate` also loads the 30 demo complaints (acceptable for the demo, say so in the RUNBOOK); Ollama tag `0.34.0` is pinned, good.

I will update RUNBOOK section 6 (seed) after this merges. Approving.

Reviewed as Taha (with Claude Code assisting), head `e602563`. CI on this head: all ten required checks and SonarCloud are green.

**I checked that the tests are real regressions:** I put this PR's `views.test.tsx` on top of the current `dev` Dashboard and ran Vitest: **2 failed / 11 passed**, and the two failures are exactly the two new tests (`hides previous filter results while loading and retriesâ€¦` and `returns to the last valid filtered pageâ€¦`). On this head all **13 pass**, `typecheck` and `lint` are clean.

The three behaviours you asked me to check, against the code:
- **Filter change hides stale rows:** `load()` now calls `setResult(null)` before the request, so during loading or after a failure no row from the previous selection sits under the new filter label. The test asserts the old complaint is gone while `Loading` is shown and again after the failure.
- **Failed request can be retried:** the alert now has a `Retry loading complaints` button that calls `load()` again with the current filters and page (the test checks the selected category is still `water` and the request contains `category=water`). Abort/version protection is untouched, so a retry cannot be overwritten by an older response.
- **Invalid final page recovers:** when the server's `total` makes the requested page too high, the component sets `page` to the last valid page and the effect reloads it; it cannot loop (after the correction `page == lastPage`). The test moves the last open row to `in_progress` from page 2 and lands on `20 complaints Â· Page 1 of 1` with `Next` disabled, requesting `page=1&status=open`. The status rules stay on the server (409 text still verbatim, existing tests still pass).

Answer to your "why hide old rows": agreed, keeping rows under a new filter label can make an operator act on the wrong selection, especially when the new request fails.

Observations, none a defect: (1) between the out-of-range response and the corrected fetch there is one render with neither rows nor the Loading text (`finally` sets loading false before the effect re-runs); a one-frame flash, not wrong data. (2) Hiding rows during the reload after a status change makes the list jump and drops keyboard focus from the select the operator just used; acceptable, a possible later polish.

Approving. Artfever can merge it.
